title: smart-retry quarantine + tenant shaping to reduce customer-facing 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a recent customer escalation, several hosted API tenants experienced correlated 5xx bursts and elevated timeouts driven by aggressive client-side retries plus a small subset of long-polling workloads that exhausted worker slots. This ticket implements a two-pronged mitigation: (1) a 'smart-retry quarantine' server-side short-circuit that detects amplification loops and throttles repeated identical requests per-tenant for a short window, and (2) a tenant-shaping policy that limits long-running KV/batch-heavy requests concurrently per tenant under load. Goals: reduce customer-visible 5xx spikes, prevent cross-tenant amplification, and enable graceful degradation for noisy tenants.
background: Incident notes: On 2026-02-20 we saw three tenants generate repeated retries after intermittent transient 502s from a specific downstream GPU pool. Retries amplified queue depth, leading to request queue saturation and cascading 504/524 timeouts for other tenants routed to the same pool. Root causes identified: (a) SDK clients used exponential retry with high concurrency and no idempotency keys for streaming/long-poll requests, (b) runtime queueing had insufficient per-tenant reservation and relied mainly on global backpressure, (c) health probes and circuit breakers had coarse granularity. Previous fixes (ENG-51789, ENG-62490) reduced some noise but did not address tenant-level amplification patterns.
proposal: 1) Smart-retry quarantine: on receipt of N retries within T seconds for the same tenant+endpoint+payload fingerprint, return a 429 with Retry-After or route to a low-cost degraded path for the next M seconds. Implement fingerprints via SHA256 of normalized request body + endpoint + idempotency token (if present). 2) Tenant shaping: enforce a new runtime admission controller cap that reserves X worker slots per tenant and enforces a per-tenant concurrent long-running request threshold that scales down when global backlog exceeds S0. 3) SDK guidance: publish immediate best-practice update recommending idempotency tokens and tuned retry jitter; push to SDKs a change that limits parallel retries for streaming endpoints by default. 4) Observability: add new metrics (tenant_retry_spike_count, tenant_quarantine_events, tenant_longrun_concurrency) and Grafana alerts with runbook references.
acceptance_criteria: When a tenant exceeds retry fingerprint threshold, runtime returns 429 with Retry-After and quarantine event is recorded
Global 95th latency and 5xx rate decrease for noisy tenant scenarios simulated in load tests (benchmarker) by >=50%
New tenant metrics appear in console dashboards and an alert fires for sustained quarantine rates
SDK update and best-practice doc published and linked in customer communications
Rollback plan validated in staging: feature flags to disable quarantine and tenant shaping independently
work_items: runtime: implement quarantine admission controller and fingerprint cache (PR #14264)
runtime: add per-tenant reserved slots and dynamic shaping policy (PR #14279)
sdk: add retry guidance and optional client-side backoff cap (PR #8812)
e2e: load test scenario to replicate amplification pattern (bench-suite/scenarios/amplify-01)
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket after incident review. Scoped quarantine + shaping as minimal invasive mitigations to avoid broad throttles.
2026-03-01 - Marco Nguyen: Prototype fingerprint cache implemented. Observed low memory overhead in canary (0.6% heap). Will iterate eviction TTL.
2026-03-03 - SRE (Liu Chen): Runbook drafted. Added explicit guidance to page on quarantine events and suggested Runbook step: 'promote tenant to reserved pool' for paying customers.
2026-03-05 - Design (Ravi Kapoor): UX for console alert cards reviewed. Recommendation: include quick links to tenant overview + last 24h retry histogram.
2026-03-07 - Customer success (Elena Torres): Drafted customer-facing KB explaining why 429s may appear during protective quarantine and recommended SDK settings to mitigate impact.

2026-03-09 - Marco Nguyen: Canary deploy to a subset of GPU pools. Observed quarantine events for two tenants; those tenants' amplified 5xx cascades subsided within 45s on average. No servicewide regressions observed.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Decision to proceed to broader rollout behind feature flags; scheduled step rollout across remaining regions next week. Leaving ticket In Progress for final QA and docs.
rollback_plan: Feature flags gate both smart-retry quarantine and tenant shaping. Rollback steps: disable flags -> monitor metrics for 30 minutes -> if regression persists, scale target GPU pools down by cordoning and draining noisy tenants. Notify CS for customer comms.
notes: This approach favors short-term protective measures with measurable observability. Longer-term work should include model-routing isolation and per-tenant reserved capacity options in Dedicated product path.
estimated_impact: Expected to reduce cross-tenant 5xx amplification windows and lower customer-visible timeouts in host pools by ~30-70% for noisy scenarios based on benchmark simulations.
